correctness.rationale: The sorted four tetrahedral cosine scores give exactly \(2(b+c)/\sqrt3\) or \(2(b-c)/\sqrt3\) depending on independent sign parity in the spherical chamber \(a\ge b\ge c\ge0\). Each of its 48 signed-permutation variants has exact area \(\pi/12\). The spherical Jacobian under the two orthogonal latitude parametrizations is \(ds\,d\phi\). The parity-conditional angular slices cancel their internal arcsine boundary terms, yielding the density \(6H(s)/\pi\). The derivative \(H\prime(s)=-1/((1-s^2)\sqrt{3-4s^2})\) integrates to the displayed CDF and elementary exact first/second moments. Every tetrahedral intervertex chord length is \(\sqrt{8/3}\), which gives the exact arcsine transformation from score gap to spherical Voronoi boundary distance. The bundled checker recomputes 48 direct chamber scores, 89 CDF quadratures, two moments, 180000 random directions, and direct angular boundary distances; all passed. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove continuous identities.

originality.rationale: The evaluated object is the probability law of the top-two score gap for a single Haar-uniform query to the regular four-word tetrahedral spherical code, equivalently the distribution of geodesic distance to the Voronoi decision set. In the primary full texts inspected, the 2015 multiprobe cross-polytope work ranks top coordinates without this tetrahedral law, while the 2019 tetrahedral code analysis evaluates a two-input collision probability by a six-dimensional orthant formula. Published closest snippets about unions of spherical caps concern the maximum score, not the joint top-two margin. The accessible earlier nearest-distance geometry of a 12-word cuboctahedral code has a different code and marginal. No covering statement was found in targeted published-finding corpus and public-literature searches; this does not establish exhaustive priority.

value.rationale: The all-threshold score gap and angular decision-boundary distance are natural quantitative-geometry invariants of a four-vertex spherical code; they directly give the measure of points robust under every perturbation of prescribed angular radius. The result is an exact full density/CDF with exact moments and strict shape rather than an arbitrary finite computation, and exhibits a nontrivial cancellation of parity-stratum transition terms. It can calibrate deterministic angular quantizer reliability without assuming any stochastic noise law.
